## 0.9 Instructor Dashboard {#sec-instructor-dashboard}

The Rguroo **Dashboard** is a set of tools for instructors. From the Dashboard, you can create groups for your classes, build your own dataset repositories, share those repositories with your students, monitor student login activity, and email your students. Students do not have access to the Dashboard, but they benefit from the repositories and emails you share with them through it.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
**Students:** This section is written for instructors. You only need Section 0.4.4 (*My Groups*) to join your instructor's group and import datasets from it.
:::

### 0.9.1 Creating Instructor Account {#sec-create-instructor-acct}

Faculty accounts in Rguroo are **free**. To register, you must use your **institution-issued email address** (for example, an address ending in .edu). The Rguroo team reviews each faculty registration manually before approving it, and accounts registered with a personal email address, such as Gmail or Yahoo, will not be approved.

Instructors register in much the same way as students (see Section 0.2), with one difference: on the registration page, select **Faculty** instead of **Student** (see @fig-rguroo-student).

1.  Go to the [Rguroo website](https://www.rguroo.com) and click **Register** in the upper-right corner.
2.  Select **Faculty**.
3.  Enter your institutional email address and complete the email verification, as described in Section 0.2 (@fig-faculty-register).
4.  Complete the **Your Information** page, including your institution's name.
5.  Click **Submit**, then check your email and complete the verification, as described in Section 0.2. Because faculty accounts are reviewed manually, approval is not immediate. You will receive an email when your account has been approved.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| label: fig-faculty-register
#| fig-cap: 'Rguroo Faculty Registration Page'
#| fig-alt: 'Rguroo Faculty Registration web page. Under the heading Register Faculty, the Your Role dropdown is set to Instructor, followed by Email and Verify Email text boxes. A note below reads: In order for your account to be approved, you must use your institution-issued email address. A yellow Submit button appears at the bottom.'
#| out-width: "80%"
knitr::include_graphics("Rguroo_outputs/Chapter_0/faculty_register.png")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
**Plan ahead.** Because faculty accounts are reviewed manually, register well before the start of the term so your account is ready in time to create your class groups and repositories.
:::

Once your faculty account is active, a **Dashboard** button appears at the top right of the Rguroo window (item [7]{.circle-number} in @fig-dashboard).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
**Already have a student or trial account?** Your faculty account must be registered with your institutional email address. If you previously created an account with a different email, register again as faculty using your institutional email.
:::

Rguroo also offers free workshops and one-on-one training for faculty. To schedule a session, visit the [Request Training](https://rguroo.com/request-training/) page.

### 0.9.2 Navigating Instructor Dashboard {#sec-navigate-dashboard}	 

To open the Dashboard, log in to Rguroo and click the **Dashboard** button at the top right of the Rguroo window. The Dashboard opens in a new browser tab.

The left side of the Dashboard has two main icons:

-   **Groups** opens the **Manage Groups** page, where you create groups, add and remove members, share repositories, monitor activity, and send emails (@fig-dashboard-groups).
-   **Repositories** opens the **Manage Repositories** page, where you create dataset repositories and add datasets to them.

On a small screen, click the three horizontal lines at the top right of the Dashboard window to see these icons.

On both pages, the left pane is a **directory** that works like the folders in your Rguroo toolboxes. You can create items in the main (root) directory or organize them in folders. For example, you might create a folder for each semester, or a folder for each course you teach. To create a folder, click the **FOLDER** button at the top of the directory pane, type a name, and click [Apply]{.button}.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
#| label: fig-dashboard-groups
#| fig-cap: 'Rguroo Dashboard Showing the Manage Groups Page'
#| fig-alt: 'Rguroo Dashboard with Welcome Instructor at the top right. The left side has two icons, Groups, which is selected, and Repositories. Next to them are the FOLDER and GROUP buttons, and below them is a folder named My Classes with a trash icon and an add group icon on its right. The main area is titled Manage Groups.'
#| out-width: "90%"
knitr::include_graphics("Rguroo_outputs/Chapter_0/dashboard_groups.png")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
**Suggested order for setting up a new class:** (1) create a repository and add your datasets ([Section 0.9.3](#sec-create-repository)), (2) create a group for the class ([Section 0.9.4(#sec-create-groups)]), (3) share the repository with the group ([Section 0.9.5](#sec-link-repository)), and (4) give students the Group Code.
:::

### 0.9.3 Creating Repositories {#sec-create-repository}

A **dataset repository** is a collection of datasets that users can import into their own Rguroo accounts with a few clicks. The Kozak repository used throughout this text is one example. Creating your own repository lets you give students exactly the datasets they need for a lab, project, or exam.

**Creating a repository**

1.  In the Dashboard, select the **Repositories** icon to open the **Manage Repositories** page.
2.  Click the REPOSITORY button at the top of the directory pane (@fig-create-repository). To create the repository inside a folder, click the plus sign next to the folder name instead.
3.  In the **Create Repository** dialog, enter a unique **Name** and, optionally, a **Description** and click CREATE.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
#| fig-cap: 'Create Repository Dialog in the Rguroo Dashboard'
#| label: fig-create-repository
#| fig-alt: 'Rguroo Dashboard with Welcome Instructor at the top right and Repositories selected on the left. Next to it are the FOLDER and REPOSITORY buttons and a folder named My Repositories. The Create Repository dialog is open in the center with an empty Name box, an empty Description box, and a CREATE button.'
#| out-width: "90%"
knitr::include_graphics("Rguroo_outputs/Chapter_0/dashboard_create_repository.png")
```

**Adding datasets to a repository**

Select the repository name to open its **Manage Repository** page (@fig-manage-repository). In the **Datasets** section, the icons on the right let you add datasets in three ways:

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| label: fig-manage-repository
#| fig-cap: 'Manage Repository Page for a New, Empty Repository'
#| fig-alt: 'Rguroo Dashboard page titled Manage Repository: New Repository. Below the title, the repository name New Repository and the note Created: a few seconds ago appear, followed by a count of 0 Datasets with a pencil edit icon and a trash icon on the right. The Datasets section below shows 0 Records found and a row of icons on the right: a download arrow, a shaded plus, a plus sign with three lines, a plain plus sign, and an up arrow to collapse the section. The empty table has columns for Name, Title, File Type, Comment, Columns, and Rows.'
#| out-width: "90%"
knitr::include_graphics("Rguroo_outputs/Chapter_0/dashboard_manage_repository.png")
```

-   **Upload a CSV or Excel file from your computer.** Click the plain plus sign (fourth icon) and select the file. Then enter:
    -   **Name**: the dataset name students will see in their **Data** toolbox after importing.
    -   **Title**: the title shown in the repository list.
    -   **Comment** (optional): a short description students see when hovering over the dataset name.
    -   **Documentation** (optional): a full description of the dataset, typed in the text editor or uploaded as a text (.txt) or HTML file. Students can open it from the information icon in the repository list. This is a good place to paste the dataset's code book.
-   **Import datasets from your own Rguroo account.** Click the plus sign with three lines (third icon), check the datasets you want from your **Data** toolbox, and click [Import]{.button}.
-   **Import datasets from a repository another instructor has shared with you.** Click the shaded plus (second icon), choose the shared repository, select the datasets, and click the import button.

| Icon | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| Down arrow (first icon) | Downloads selected datasets to your computer |
| Shaded plus (second icon) | Imports datasets from a repository another instructor shared with you |
| Plus with three lines (third icon) | Imports datasets from your own Rguroo account |
| Plain plus (fourth icon) | Uploads a CSV or Excel file from your computer |

: Icons in the Datasets section of the Manage Repository page {#tbl-repository-icons tbl-alt="Table describing the four icons in the Datasets section of the Rguroo Manage Repository page: the down arrow downloads selected datasets, the shaded plus imports datasets from a repository shared by another instructor, the plus with three lines imports datasets from your own Rguroo account, and the plain plus uploads a CSV or Excel file from your computer."}



**Managing datasets in a repository**

Each dataset in the list has a download icon and an eye icon for previewing it. Hover over a dataset name to see the eye icon (preview) and the down-arrow icon (download). To delete or update a dataset, check the box next to its name. A bar appears at the bottom of the page with the buttons **DELETE SELECTED DATASET** and **UPDATE DATASET DETAILS** (@fig-manage-datasets). Use **UPDATE DATASET DETAILS** to change a dataset’s name, title, comment, or documentation. To rename a repository or change its description, click the pencil icon next to the dataset count. To delete a repository, click the trash icon next to it.

A bar at the bottom of the page reads 1 selected, with the buttons DELETE SELECTED DATASET and UPDATE DATASET DETAILS.'
```{r, echo = FALSE}
#| out-width: "90%"

```

### 0.9.4 Creating Groups {#sec-create-groups}

A **group** is a set of Rguroo users, usually the students in one of your classes. Groups are how you share repositories with students, monitor their activity, and send them emails.

**Creating a group**

1.  In the Dashboard, select the **Groups** icon to open the **Manage Groups** page.
2.  Click the **GROUP** button at the top of the directory pane (@fig-create-group), or click the add-group icon next to a folder name to create the group inside that folder. You can also duplicate an existing group using the duplicate button.
3.  In the **Create Group** dialog, enter:
    -   **Name**: for example, *STAT C1000 Section 12345 Fall 2026*.
    -   **Group Code**: the code students will type to join. Type your own alphanumeric code or click [Generate]{.button} for a random one. Rguroo will ask for a different code if yours is already in use.
    -   **Description** (optional).
    -   **Expiration Date**: the date the group expires. The default is six months after the group is created. After the group expires, members can no longer access the repositories shared with the group, although any datasets they already imported stay in their accounts.
and click **CREATE**

```{r, echo = FALSE}
#| label: fig-create-group
#| fig-cap: 'Create Group Dialog in the Rguroo Dashboard'
#| fig-alt: 'Rguroo Dashboard with Welcome Instructor at the top right and Groups selected on the left. Next to it are the FOLDER and GROUP buttons and a folder named My Classes with a trash icon and an add group icon. The Create Group dialog is open in the center with an empty Name box, a Group Code box with a GENERATE button, an empty Description box, an Expiration Date box showing 2027/04/13, and a CREATE button.'
#| out-width: "90%"
knitr::include_graphics("Rguroo_outputs/Chapter_0/dashboard_create_group.png")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
⚠️ The Group Code cannot be changed after the group is created. You can change the group's name, description, and expiration date at any time by selecting the group and clicking the edit icon.
:::

**Adding students to a group**

There are two ways to add members:

-   **Students join with the Group Code.** Give students the Group Code (for example, in your syllabus or course website). Students join by clicking *My Groups* at the top of the Rguroo window, selecting *Join a Group*, entering the code, and clicking *Join Group*, as described in Section 0.4.4.
-   **You invite students by email.** Select the group, then in the **Members** section click the plus sign, enter the student's Rguroo username (email), and click [Add]{.button}. To invite a whole class at once, click the plus-sign-with-three-lines button, download the CSV or Excel template, fill in your students' email addresses, and import the completed file. Each student receives an email with the Group Code and instructions for joining.


### 0.9.5 Linking Repositories to Groups {#sec-link-repository}

Creating a repository does not automatically give students access to it. You need to **share** (link) the repository with a group.

1.  In the Dashboard, select the **Groups** icon and click the name of the group.
2.  At the bottom of the page, find the section labeled **Share My Repositories** and click the down arrow to see the repositories you have created.
3.  In the **Action** column, click the share button in the row for the repository you want to share.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
#| label: fig-share-repo-group
#| fig-cap: 'Sharing a Repository with a Group'
#| fig-alt: 'Rguroo Dashboard Manage Group page for New Group, which is highlighted in the left sidebar below a folder named My Classes. The page shows the group code, an expiration date of in 6 months, 0 members, and 1 Shared out of 1 Repositories. Below an empty Members section, the Share My Repositories section lists New Repository with a green SHARED status and an UNSHARE button in the Actions column.'
#| out-width: "90%"
knitr::include_graphics("Rguroo_outputs/Chapter_0/dashboard_share_repo_group.png")
```

The **Status** column changes to show that the repository is shared, and the share button changes to an unshare button. To stop sharing the repository with that group, click the unshare button. You can share the same repository with several groups, which is useful when you teach more than one section of the same course.

Students can then import the shared datasets in either of two ways:

-   Click *My Groups* and select *Show My Groups*, then select the group and repository (see Section 0.4.4).
-   In the **Data** toolbox, select [Data Import]{.dpd} then [Dataset Repository]{.fun}, choose the **My Repositories** option, and select the repository.

**Sharing a repository with another instructor**

Repositories can also be shared directly with other faculty, even if they are not in one of your groups. This is a convenient way for a department to share a common set of datasets. In the **Repositories** page, hover over the repository and click the share icon. In the **Share Repository** dialog (@fig-share-repo-dialog), type the instructor’s Rguroo username (email) in the Email of user to add box, click the plus icon, and then click **SHARE**. To stop sharing, click the trash icon next to their name. Students can only be given access to repositories through groups.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
#| label: fig-share-repo-faculty
#| fig-cap: 'Share Icon for a Repository in the Repositories Sidebar'
#| fig-alt: 'Rguroo Dashboard Repositories sidebar showing a folder named My Repositories and a repository named New Repository. The mouse is over New Repository, revealing a share icon and a copy icon on the right, with a tooltip reading Share New Repository.'
#| out-width: "50%"
knitr::include_graphics("Rguroo_outputs/Chapter_0/dashboard_share_repo_faculty.png")
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
#| label: fig-share-repo-dialog
#| fig-cap: 'Share Repository Dialog for Sharing with Another Instructor'
#| fig-alt: 'Rguroo Share Repository dialog with a text box labeled Email of user to add and a plus icon, the message This repository is not shared with anyone, and a SHARE button.'
#| out-width: "60%"
knitr::include_graphics("Rguroo_outputs/Chapter_0/dashboard_share_repo_dialog.png")
```

### 0.9.6 Student Activity Log {#sec-student-activity}

The Dashboard lets you see when, and for how long, each group member has been logged in to Rguroo. This can help you check whether students are getting started with Rguroo early in the term, or follow up with a student who has not logged in.

1.  In the Dashboard, select the **Groups** icon and click the name of the group. A list of group members appears.
2.  Move your mouse over a student's name and click the activity monitor icon.
3.  A time plot opens showing the dates the student logged in along the horizontal axis and how long they were logged in each time.

The member list also provides two other tools:

-   **Emailing students.** Check the box next to the **Name** header to select everyone, or check individual students. Click the send-mail button at the bottom of the page, enter a subject and message, and click send. Emails come from a no-reply address, so ask students to contact you through your usual channels rather than replying.
-   **Removing students.** Select the students' names and click the remove-members button at the bottom of the list. Removed students immediately lose access to the repositories shared with the group.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
The activity log shows **login activity** only. It does not show which datasets a student opened or which analyses they ran. To see a student's actual Rguroo work, ask them to submit an RGR file (see Section 0.6.4).
:::

### 0.9.7 Applets and Calculators {#sec-applets-calculators}

The **Applets-Calculators** toolbox on the left side of the Rguroo window contains interactive tools that are useful for in-class demonstrations and for students exploring probability and inference concepts on their own. All Rguroo users, not just instructors, have access to this toolbox.

To open an applet, click **Applets-Calculators** on the left side of the Rguroo window, expand a folder by clicking the plus sign next to it, and double-click the applet you want. You can also type part of an applet's name in the **Search Applet** box to narrow the list (@fig-applets).

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| label: fig-applets
#| fig-cap: 'Applets-Calculators Toolbox'
#| fig-alt: 'Rguroo Applets-Calculators toolbox expanded below the Data, Plots, Analytics, Prediction-Classification, and Probability-Simulation toolboxes. A Search Applet box appears above an Applets list containing three folders. The Art of Stat folder contains Exploratory Data Analysis, Association and Correlation, Distributions, Central Limit Theorem, two Confidence Intervals folders, and Inference for Comparing groups. The Rossman/Chance folder contains Sampling Distribution, Data Analysis, Probability, and Statistical Inference. The Calculators (Desmos) folder contains Scientific Calculator, Four Function Calculator, and Graphical Calculator.'
#| out-width: "40%"
knitr::include_graphics("Rguroo_outputs/Chapter_0/applets_calculators.png")
```

The toolbox is organized into three folders:

-   **Art of Stat.** Applets that accompany the *Statistics: The Art and Science of Learning from Data* textbook, organized by topic: Exploratory Data Analysis; Association and Correlation; Distributions; the Central Limit Theorem; Confidence Intervals and Significance Tests; and Inference for Comparing Groups.
-   **Rossman/Chance.** Well-known teaching applets organized into four areas: Sampling Distribution, Data Analysis, Probability, and Statistical Inference. They are especially useful for simulation-based demonstrations, such as showing how a sampling distribution builds up as more samples are drawn.
-   **Calculators (Desmos).** Three Desmos calculators: a **Scientific Calculator**, a **Four Function Calculator**, and a **Graphical Calculator**. The Scientific Calculator can also be opened from the Quick Access Tools menu (see Section 0.7.1). Chapter 4 uses its [func]{.dpd} menu to compute factorials, permutations ($_nP_r$), and combinations ($_nC_r$).

[Walkthrough Example: Using the Desmos Scientific Calculator]{style="color: blue; font-weight: bold;"}

A class of 30 students needs to choose a 3-person committee. Use the Desmos Scientific Calculator in Rguroo to find the number of possible committees.

**Let's Use the Calculator:** Open the **Applets-Calculators** toolbox, expand the **Calculators (Desmos)** folder, and double-click **Scientific Calculator**. Click the [func]{.dpd} button and select **nCr**. Type [30, 3]{.typein} and the calculator displays **4,060** (@fig-desmos-ncr). There are 4,060 possible committees. You will learn why this is a combination, and when to use one, in Chapter 4.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| label: fig-desmos-ncr
#| fig-cap: 'Computing a Combination with the Desmos Scientific Calculator in Rguroo'
#| fig-alt: 'Desmos Scientific Calculator open in a Rguroo tab named Scientific Calculator. The input line reads nCr(30,3) with the answer equals 4060 on the right. Below the input line, the func tab is selected, showing buttons for sin, cos, tan, their inverses, mean, stdev, stdevp, nPr, nCr, and factorial, along with exponent, square root, absolute value, round, natural log, log, e, and pi buttons.'
#| out-width: "70%"
knitr::include_graphics("Rguroo_outputs/Chapter_0/desmos_ncr.png")
```

![Try It](Rguroo_Icons/try_it.png){width=45px} **Try It: Use the Desmos Scientific Calculator**

Open the Desmos Scientific Calculator in Rguroo and use the [func]{.dpd} tab to complete each calculation.

a.  A coffee shop offers 8 pastries. Find $8!$, the number of ways to arrange all 8 pastries in a display case, using the **!** button.
b.  A club with 10 members needs to choose a president, vice president, secretary, and treasurer. Find the number of ways to fill these four positions using **nPr** with $n = 10$ and $r = 4$.
c.  Recall the six values in the *Study Hours 6* dataset: 6, 10, 8, 5, 12, 9. Use **mean** and **stdev** to find the mean and sample standard deviation, separating the values with commas. Compare your answers with the Rguroo report you created in Section 0.6.4.
